Chapter 6.description: Chapter 6 is a multi-faceted chapter within a thesis and associated papers, primarily centered on the validation and application of a time-domain Discontinuous Galerkin (DG) wave-based solver for acoustic simulations. The chapter corresponds to Paper V, where this solver is applied to a real open-office environment, and it also serves to validate the developed solver. Beyond numerical validation, Chapter 6 presents a subjective study on the perception of low-frequency modal distribution, specifically investigating how changes in this distribution are perceived and how this perception depends on room aspect ratios. This study employs a derived model and a test method similar to a previous chapter that raised issues about cues enabling detection between rooms with different modal distributions. The chapter also confirms Bucklein's finding that detection of modal changes is only possible when played tones fall within the region of the resonance. Furthermore, the chapter describes the technical setup used in the study, including a binaural model and a Butterworth high-pass filter.

Chapter 8.description: Chapter 8 is a chapter within a research thesis and paper that focuses on the perceptual and experimental study of room acoustics, specifically investigating the difference limen (DL) for the Q-factor of room modes in the presence of music signals. The chapter presents a detailed procedure for extracting this difference limen, while also examining the effects of mid-frequency reverberation time on perception. It defines the difference limen for reverberation time and explores perceptible changes in the Q-factor of room modes, thereby contributing to the understanding of how listeners detect alterations in acoustic resonance. The chapter also describes the experimental system and techniques used for measuring these difference limens, and it includes data that were analyzed using ANOVA and trend tests, with normal distributions obtained for the collected data. Notably, the chapter contains experimental data from a specific "Run number 3" and is positioned within the broader research as a section that contradicts some of Toole's remarks on resonance perception, offering an alternative or refined perspective on how resonances are perceived in audio environments.
